newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher, led by Ganadero.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher, led by Ganadero.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher as Banco Ganadero snapped its recent losing streak and posted solid gains in Bogota and Medellin.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up 0.23 percent to close at 13,307.15 on a below-average trading volume of 659.3 million pesos.
But Bogota's IBB index ended up 0.82 percent at 855.54 on an active volume of 2.6 billion pesos.
A large cross-trade in the shares of Banco Anglo Colombiano accounted for 1.6 billion pesos of the trading volume in Bogota.
Brokers said the market mover in Bogota was Banco Ganadero, however, which closed up 3.33 percent at 279 pesos per share.

Ganadero, the country's No. 1 bank in terms of assets, fell sharply on profit-taking following its equity sale late last month. But traders said a virtual army of bottom-fishers were now stepping up to buy on the dips.
Other gainers in Bogota included brewer Bavaria SA, which closed up 1.1 percent at 3,802 pesos a share, and Banco de Bogota, which gained 0.17 percent to end at 5,710 pesos a share.
"The share prices of Bavaria and Banco de Bogota are below their book value," one broker said in a telephone interview.
"Bavaria has show that it can trade between 3,500 and 4,000 pesos a share and people know that, so it lends itself to speculation," he said.
He added that Banco de Bogota had risen on speculation that the bank's earnings will improve in the second half following the recent sale of its stake in cement maker Industrias e Inversiones Samper.
Gainers in Medellin were led by Ganadero, which rose 2.03 percent to close at 275.50 pesos a share, and Bavaria, which closed up 0.79 percent at 3,800 per share.
